explanation: Direct eye contact is expected in France and reads as sincerity, confidence, and engagement, both socially and in business. Avoiding it can come across as evasive or disinterested; French communication norms treat steady eye contact as a basic sign of respect for the person speaking.
local_tip: Maintain steady eye contact during greetings and key points of conversation, but don't make it an unbroken stare — brief natural breaks are normal.

also_check.note: Prolonged direct eye contact can feel intense or disrespectful; briefer glances, especially toward superiors, are more comfortable.
Sustained eye contact with elders or superiors can be seen as challenging; a more deferential, softer gaze is preferred in hierarchical settings.
Direct eye contact is generally read as honesty and attentiveness, similar to France.
